I’m the principal at the high school, so my days are pretty structured, but my eating feels completely out of control. About once or twice a week—sometimes more—I’ll have these episodes in the evenings, and this has been going on for at least three or four months now.

It usually happens after I get home, once my husband has gone to bed or is in another room. I’ll stand in the kitchen and just keep going: leftovers, cereal, ice cream, anything. It’s way more than anyone would normally eat in that amount of time. I keep eating even after I feel painfully full—like I have to loosen my waistband and lie down—but I still keep picking at food. I always do it alone because I’m mortified by how much I’m eating and how fast. I hide the packaging in the outside trash so my family doesn’t see.

Sometimes I do get short bursts of extra energy—maybe I stay up late reorganizing my office or talking more than usual—but they’re mild and never last more than a day or so. They don’t affect my job or judgment the way I’ve heard real mood episodes can. The eating is what feels truly out of control.
